messages.subject: Testing for invariance
parts:
Dear lavaan-group

l have a few questions regarding invariance testing.
The questions are more SEM related, so I posted them also on SEMNET, but I hope they could be of interest also for this group.

The initial position is the following: I have the factor loadings from a CFA and an EFA for a psychometric test but no raw data.
I used the test for a different sample and want to check for invariance.
I want to avoid the Procrustes rotation and had the idea to constrain my own model with the known factor loadings.
On SEMNET the proposals were first to estimate the factor loadings and CIs for my sample and compare them to the results of the CFA respectively the EFA. Second to constrain my model with the known factor loadings and have a look whether these constraints are reasonable. I like the idea but I am not sure how to constrain with the factor loadings in lavaan and missed maybe something in the documentation...

Another proposal was to calculate the variance/covariance matrix from the factor loadings and do a "simple" multi group comparison. I thought to generate the matrix I would need the standard errors and I did not find any literature regarding this idea. Do you know any and maybe even a software or do you think calculating the matrix is not posible under these circumstances.

I hope it is okay to post this in this group and would be very thankful for any help.

All the best

Petra

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Testing for invariance
parts: The questions are more SEM related, so I posted them also on SEMNET, but I hope they could be of interest also for this group.

I think the best advice you got on SEMNET was to reconstruct the model-implied covariance matrix from the estimates of the old data (or see if they provide, or would provide upon request, the observed covariance matrix).  Then you can treat that as group 1, and simply calculate the covariance matrix for your own observed data to treat as group 2.  If you save these 2 covariance matrices in a list, you can pass them to lavaan() via the sample.cov argument, and specify the sample sizes in a vector via the sample.nobs argument.  

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cov.html

Then you can test invariance across samples.
